OVERVIEW

Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We create platforms and tools, powered by AI, that deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.

We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices. Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

Highlights from fiscal year 2025 compared with fiscal year 2024 included:

•

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion.

•

Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased 14% driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue growth of 15%.

•

Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased 11% driven by Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue growth of 11%.

•

LinkedIn revenue increased 9%.

•

Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased 15% driven by Dynamics 365 revenue growth of 19%.

•

Server products and cloud services revenue increased 23% driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

•

Windows OEM and Devices revenue increased 3%.

•

Xbox content and services revenue increased 16%.

•

Search and news advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 20%.

We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices. Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

Highlights from fiscal year 2024 compared with fiscal year 2023 included:

•

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $137.4 billion.

•

Office Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased 4% and Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers grew to 82.5 million.

•

LinkedIn revenue increased 9%.

•

Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased 19% driven by Dynamics 365 growth of 24%.

•

Server products and cloud services revenue increased 22% driven by Azure and other cloud services growth of 30%.

•

•

Devices revenue decreased 15%.

We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 142% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by demand for our Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 9% from a year ago, driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 21% from a year ago, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative AI-powered design, simulation, and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 55% from a year ago, driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 68% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by the major platform shifts – accelerated computing and AI.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41% from a year ago, driven by strong Blackwell demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 70% from a year ago, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell as well as the launch of our new DGX Spark.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 39% from a year ago, driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin decreased in fiscal year 2026 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions. The gross margin decrease was also impacted by a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 were up 41% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs.

We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 142% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by demand for our Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 9% from a year ago, driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 21% from a year ago, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative AI-powered design, simulation, and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 55% from a year ago, driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 68% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by the major platform shifts – accelerated computing and AI.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41% from a year ago, driven by strong Blackwell demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 70% from a year ago, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell as well as the launch of our new DGX Spark.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 39% from a year ago, driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin decreased in fiscal year 2026 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions. The gross margin decrease was also impacted by a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 were up 41% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs.

answer:
Apple's total gross margin percentage in fiscal 2024 was 46.2% [AAPL 10-K #96].

Operating margin is calculated by dividing operating income by total revenue. Based on these figures, the implied operating margin for fiscal year 2025 is approximately 45.62%.

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 68% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by the major platform shifts – accelerated computing and AI.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41% from a year ago, driven by strong Blackwell demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 70% from a year ago, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell as well as the launch of our new DGX Spark.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 39% from a year ago, driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin decreased in fiscal year 2026 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions. The gross margin decrease was also impacted by a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 were up 41% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs.

Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We create platforms and tools, powered by AI, that deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.

We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices. Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $137.4 billion.

Question:
Comparing their respective fiscal 2024 annual reports, how much did Apple and Microsoft each spend on research and development, and which company spent more?

answer:
Based on the provided 2024 Form 10-K, Apple identifies several major categories of risk that could adversely impact its business, results of operations, and financial condition:

*   **Economic and Geopolitical Risks:** The company faces risks from global or regional economic uncertainty, which can impact demand for its products, the financial stability of its partners, and the company's own liquidity and access to credit [AAPL 10-K #15]. Additionally, the company is subject to risks from political events, international disputes, geopolitical tensions, conflict, terrorism, natural disasters, public health issues (such as pandemics), and industrial accidents [AAPL 10-K #15, #20].
*   **Operational and Supply Chain Risks:** Apple relies on outsourcing partners for manufacturing and logistics, many of which are located outside the U.S. [AAPL 10-K #26]. Business interruptions at these sources—exacerbated by the company's reliance on single or limited sources for critical components—can lead to significant expenditures, lost sales, and the need for substantial recovery time [AAPL 10-K #20].
*   **Product and Market Competition Risks:** To remain competitive, the company must manage frequent product and service transitions [AAPL 10-K #26]. Risks in this area include market acceptance, production ramp-up issues, inventory management, and the possibility that new offerings may produce lower revenues and profit margins than existing ones [AAPL 10-K #26]. The company also notes that it generates a significant portion of its net sales from a single product, making it vulnerable to declines in demand for that specific product [AAPL 10-K #69].
*   **Retail Operations Risks:** The company’s retail stores are subject to risks including macroeconomic factors, the ability to manage construction and operating costs, relationships with retail partners, inventory value fluctuations, and the ability to secure leases in quality locations [AAPL 10-K #50].
*   **Legal and Regulatory Risks:** Apple is subject to various legal proceedings and government investigations, the number and magnitude of which have generally increased over time [AAPL 10-K #50]. Question:
Across the risk factors section of Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K, what are the major categories of risk the company discusses?

answer:
Based on the provided 2024 Form 10-K, Apple categorizes its risks into several major areas:

*   **Economic and Market Risks:** The company faces risks from global or regional economic conditions, which can impact demand for products and services, affect channel partners and suppliers, and lead to financial instability or insolvency [AAPL 10-K #15]. Additionally, the company is subject to risks associated with fluctuations in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to other currencies, which can impact gross margins [AAPL 10-K #69].
*   **Operational and Supply Chain Risks:** Apple relies on outsourcing partners for manufacturing and logistics, many of which are located outside the U.S. [AAPL 10-K #26]. Business interruptions—caused by factors such as natural disasters, public health issues (e.g., pandemics), industrial accidents, or failures of logistics/supply partners—can lead to significant expenditures and lost sales [AAPL 10-K #20, #69]. The company also faces risks related to managing inventory levels and purchase commitments [AAPL 10-K #26].
*   **Product and Service Innovation Risks:** To remain competitive, the company must successfully manage the frequent introduction and transition of products and services [AAPL 10-K #26]. This involves risks related to market acceptance, production ramp-ups, and the possibility that new offerings may result in lower revenues and profit margins [AAPL 10-K #26].
*   **Retail Risks:** Retail operations are subject to macroeconomic factors, the ability to manage construction and operating costs, relationships with retail partners, and the ability to secure leases in quality locations [AAPL 10-K #50].
*   **Legal and Regulatory Risks:** The company is subject to various legal proceedings, government investigations, and potential indemnification obligations, the number and magnitude of which have generally increased over time [AAPL 10-K #50].
*   **Geopolitical and External Event Risks:** The company’s business can be materially adversely affected by political events, international disputes, geopolitical tensions, conflict, terrorism, and other business interruptions [AAPL 10-K #15].

Question:
Across the risk factors section of Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K, what are the major categories of risk the company discusses?

answer:
Based on the provided 2024 Form 10-K, Apple identifies several major categories of risk that could adversely impact its business, results of operations, and financial condition:

*   **Economic and Geopolitical Risks:** The company faces risks from global or regional economic uncertainty, which can impact demand for products and services, affect channel partners and suppliers, and lead to financial instability or reduced liquidity [AAPL 10-K #15]. Additionally, the company is subject to risks from political events, international disputes, geopolitical tensions, conflict, terrorism, natural disasters, public health issues (such as pandemics), and industrial accidents [AAPL 10-K #15, #20].
*   **Operational and Supply Chain Risks:** Apple relies on single or limited sources for critical components and depends on outsourcing partners for manufacturing and logistics, many of which are located outside the U.S. [AAPL 10-K #20, #26]. Business interruptions at these sources can lead to significant expenditures, lost sales, and recovery time [AAPL 10-K #20].
*   **Product and Competitive Risks:** To remain competitive, the company must manage frequent product and service transitions and introductions [AAPL 10-K #26]. Risks include market acceptance, production ramp-up issues, inventory management, and the possibility that new offerings may yield lower revenues or profit margins [AAPL 10-K #26]. The company also notes that a significant portion of its net sales is derived from a single product, making it vulnerable to declines in demand for that specific item [AAPL 10-K #69].
*   **Retail Risks:** Retail operations are subject to risks such as managing construction and operating costs, maintaining relationships with retail partners, managing inventory value fluctuations, and securing leases in quality locations [AAPL 10-K #50].
*   **Legal and Regulatory Risks:** The company is subject to various legal proceedings, government investigations, and potential indemnification obligations, the frequency and magnitude of which have generally increased over time [AAPL 10-K #50].
*   **Financial Risks:** The company faces risks related to foreign exchange rate fluctuations, which can impact non-U.S. dollar-denominated sales, costs, and gross margins [AAPL 10-K #69]. Other financial risks include credit and collectibility risks on trade receivables and potential limitations on the ability to issue new debt [AAPL 10-K #15].

answer:

*   **Productivity and Business Processes:** Revenue growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [MSFT 10-K #123].
*   **More Personal Computing:** Revenue growth was driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising [MSFT 10-K #123].

answer:
According to the MD&A in Microsoft's fiscal 2025 10-K, revenue increased by $36.6 billion, or 15%, with growth across each of its segments [MSFT 10-K #123]. The main drivers of this growth by segment were as follows:

*   **Intelligent Cloud:** Revenue growth was driven by Azure [MSFT 10-K #123].
*   **Productivity and Business Processes:** Revenue growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [MSFT 10-K #123].
*   **More Personal Computing:** Revenue growth was driven by Gaming and Search and news advertising [MSFT 10-K #123].

In its fiscal 2026 annual report, NVIDIA highlights several principal categories of risk, including:

*   **Industry and Market Risks:** The company faces risks related to the failure to meet evolving industry needs, rapid technological changes, and the requirement to adapt strategies to address disruptive innovations or shifts in industry standards [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Operational and Product Risks:** NVIDIA faces challenges regarding product quality, production issues, and inventory management, such as inventory provisions for low-yielding materials [NVDA 10-K #58]. The company also notes that product transitions are difficult and may impact demand predictability and supply mix [NVDA 10-K #58].
*   **Acquisitions and Investments:** Risks include the inability to realize potential benefits from acquisitions or investments, challenges in integrating acquired companies, and potential regulatory hurdles that could reduce the value of such transactions [NVDA 10-K #84].
*   **Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Risks:** The company is subject to risks involving data privacy and security laws, litigation, investigations, and regulatory proceedings [NVDA 10-K #43]. Additionally, NVIDIA faces potential financial harm from tax liabilities and changes in tax laws [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Intellectual Property and Governance:** Protecting intellectual property rights is noted as a costly endeavor, and the company acknowledges that certain provisions in its governing documents and agreements could delay or prevent a change in control [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Environmental and Social Risks:** NVIDIA faces reputational and financial risks related to the responsible use of its technologies, including AI [NVDA 10-K #43]. Furthermore, the company faces risks related to business trends influenced by climate change, specifically concerns regarding the high absolute energy requirements of its GPUs [NVDA 10-K #84].

answer:
In its fiscal 2026 annual report, NVIDIA highlights several principal categories of risk, including:

*   **Industry and Market Risks:** The company faces risks related to the failure to meet evolving industry needs, rapid technological changes, and the need to adapt strategies to address disruptive innovations [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Operational and Product Risks:** NVIDIA faces risks regarding product quality or production issues, which can lead to inventory provisions, warranty costs, or product delays [NVDA 10-K #58]. Additionally, the company faces challenges in managing supply chain costs, predicting demand, and navigating complex product transitions [NVDA 10-K #58].
*   **Acquisition and Investment Risks:** The company may not realize the benefits of business investments or acquisitions, and the inability to successfully integrate acquired companies could negatively impact growth and financial results [NVDA 10-K #84]. Regulatory challenges and delays in completing acquisitions can also reduce the anticipated benefits of such transactions [NVDA 10-K #84].
*   **Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance Risks:** NVIDIA is subject to risks involving data privacy and security laws, litigation, investigations, and regulatory proceedings [NVDA 10-K #43]. The company also faces potential financial harm from tax liabilities, changes in tax laws, and issues related to the responsible use of AI [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Intellectual Property Risks:** Protecting intellectual property rights is costly, and the company’s ability to compete could be harmed if it is unsuccessful in these efforts or if it is prohibited from manufacturing or selling its products [NVDA 10-K #43].
*   **Climate Change and Environmental Risks:** The company faces risks related to business trends influenced by climate change, specifically concerns regarding the high absolute energy requirements of its GPUs [NVDA 10-K #84].
*   **Governance Risks:** Provisions in governing documents, Delaware law, and agreements with Microsoft could delay or prevent a change in control [NVDA 10-K #43].

Question:
How did Apple return capital to shareholders in fiscal 2025, and how much did it spend on dividends and share repurchases?

answer:
In fiscal 2025, Apple returned capital to shareholders through the payment of dividends and the repurchase of common stock [AAPL 10-K #110].

Based on the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the year ended September 27, 2025:
*   **Dividends:** The company spent $15,421 million on payments for dividends and dividend equivalents [AAPL 10-K #110].
*   **Share Repurchases:** The company spent $90,711 million on the repurchases of common stock [AAPL 10-K #110].

Productivity and Business Processes

Revenue increased $14.0 billion or 13%.

Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $10.8 billion or 14%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 15% with Microsoft 365 Commercial seat growth of 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings, as well as growth in revenue per user. •

Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased $756 million or 11%. Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue grew 11% driven by Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriber growth of 8% to 89.0 million, as well as growth in revenue per user from the price increase announced in January 2025.

•

LinkedIn revenue increased $1.4 billion or 9% with growth across all lines of business.

•

Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased $996 million or 15% driven by growth in Dynamics 365, offset in part by a decline in Dynamics on-premises products. Dynamics 365 revenue grew 19% with growth across all workloads.

Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. We create platforms and tools, powered by AI, that deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.

We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices. Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

Highlights from fiscal year 2024 compared with fiscal year 2023 included:

•

Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $137.4 billion.

•

Office Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased 14% driven by Office 365 Commercial growth of 16%.

•

Office Consumer products and cloud services revenue increased 4% and Microsoft 365 Consumer subscribers grew to 82.5 million.

•

LinkedIn revenue increased 9%.

•

Dynamics products and cloud services revenue increased 19% driven by Dynamics 365 growth of 24%.

•

Server products and cloud services revenue increased 22% driven by Azure and other cloud services growth of 30%.

•

Windows revenue increased 8% with Windows original equipment manufacturer licensing (“Windows OEM”) revenue growth of 7% and Windows Commercial products and cloud services revenue growth of 11%.

•

Devices revenue decreased 15%.

We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 142% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by demand for our Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 9% from a year ago, driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 21% from a year ago, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative AI-powered design, simulation, and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 55% from a year ago, driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

Critical Accounting Estimates

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 68% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by the major platform shifts – accelerated computing and AI.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41% from a year ago, driven by strong Blackwell demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 142% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by demand for our Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 9% from a year ago, driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 21% from a year ago, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative AI-powered design, simulation, and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 55% from a year ago, driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications. These platforms incorporate processors, interconnects, software, algorithms, systems, and services to deliver unique value. Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

Revenue for fiscal year 2025 was $130.5 billion, up 114% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 142% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by demand for our Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform used for large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications. We began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 9% from a year ago, driven by sales of our GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 21% from a year ago, driven by the continued ramp of Ada RTX GPU workstations for use cases such as generative AI-powered design, simulation, and engineering.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2025 was up 55% from a year ago, driven by sales of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin increased in fiscal year 2025 driven by a higher mix of Data Center revenue.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2025 were up 45% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compensation increases, and engineering development, compute and infrastructure costs for new product introductions.

Revenue for fiscal year 2026 was $215.9 billion, up 65% from a year ago.

Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 68% from a year ago. The strong year-on-year growth was driven by the major platform shifts – accelerated computing and AI.

Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 41% from a year ago, driven by strong Blackwell demand. We expect supply constraints to be a headwind to Gaming in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and beyond.

Professional Visualization revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 70% from a year ago, driven by exceptional demand for Blackwell as well as the launch of our new DGX Spark.

Automotive revenue for fiscal year 2026 was up 39% from a year ago, driven by continued adoption of our self-driving platforms.

Gross margin decreased in fiscal year 2026 as our business model transitioned from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions. The gross margin decrease was also impacted by a $4.5 billion charge associated with H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations.

Operating expenses for fiscal year 2026 were up 41% from a year ago, driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses due to employee growth and compute and infrastructure costs.

answer: Apple's total net sales were $391,035 million in fiscal 2024, compared to $383,285 million in fiscal 2023 [AAPL 10-K #95]. This represents an increase of 2% [AAPL 10-K #95].
